title: submitnow Pricing, Free Quotas & Self-Hosting
shortAnswer: submitnow is $0 forever with no account or credit card required. Both the hosted web workbench at www.submitnow.dev and the MIT open-source CLI/MCP server are completely free for personal, agency, and commercial use; hosted endpoints enforce only per-IP fair-use rate limits to prevent abuse, while running submitnow locally or self-hosted removes those hosted limits completely.

boundarySection.heading: Why is submitnow free when competing IndexNow tools charge $9–$59/month?
paragraphs: The IndexNow protocol itself is a free, open standard backed by Bing, Yandex, Seznam.cz, Naver, and Yep. submitnow stays $0 forever because it runs statelessly without maintaining a multi-tenant user database, persistent crawl logs, or background cron pollers.

Commercial platforms charge $9–$59/month primarily for cloud-hosted scheduled sitemap watchers, long-term delivery analytics, and team alerting. If you already run deploys through GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers, or an AI coding agent with MCP, submitnow gives you the same upstream IndexNow reach at $0 recurring cost.

faq.question: Is submitnow really free, or is there a hidden URL cap?
faq.answer: submitnow is genuinely $0 with no account wall and no 200-URL/day cap. On the hosted site, per-IP sliding-window limits (30 batch submissions, 60 key checks, and 20 remote sitemap fetches per 10 minutes) exist solely to protect outbound infrastructure from abuse. Because each batch can carry up to 10,000 URLs, normal sites and migrations run comfortably within the free hosted tier.

faq.question: Can agencies and commercial teams use submitnow?
faq.answer: Yes. Both the hosted workbench at www.submitnow.dev and the MIT-licensed repository (overstarry/submitnow) are free for commercial, enterprise, and SEO agency workflows.

faq.question: How do I run high-volume automation without hosted IP rate limits?
faq.answer: Clone the MIT repository and run node cli/submitnow.ts directly inside GitHub Actions or your backend, connect node mcp/server.ts to Claude Code/Cursor/Antigravity, or self-host the Next.js app with custom INDEXNOW_SUBMIT_RATE_LIMIT environment variables.

faq.question: Does submitnow offer an SLA or guaranteed search engine indexing?
faq.answer: No. submitnow is provided as-is under the MIT license without commercial SLA guarantees, and the IndexNow protocol itself signals URL discovery rather than guaranteeing search engine indexing or ranking.
